title: DOC: Converted atoms and calculators to sphinx #1767
body:
Converted the atoms and calculators tutorial to Sphinx gallery #1767.


- Changed the calculator used from GPAW to EMT since this tutorial is supposed to be one of the first introductory tutorial and the external calculators are being discussed later in a separate tutorial. This also simplifies the whole tutorial since a lot of discussion was previously about the parameters used and the periodic boundary conditions necessary. 
- Instead of having exercise sections in between the tutorial with the solution at the end, I implemented the content of these exercises into the tutorial directly for a nicer reading flow.
- Added deprication warning to the old tutorial.
- Modified pyproject.toml to exclude certain ruff rules for this tutorial
author: DBodesheim

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
This forgets to close the trajectory.  It should do:

```
with Trajectory('mytrajectory.traj', 'w') as traj:
    traj.write(atoms)
```

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: All the code using traj should be inside a `with` block

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I think we need `For the full list, run::` with double-colon at the end in order to tell it that the following text is code.  (Applies to all commands)

Otherwise it thinks the indented text is a quote, and it formats `--formats` into a single `–formats` which has an *en-dash* instead of two hyphens, and thus fail when pasted into a terminal.

Apologies @DBodesheim I didn't spot this in the previous round.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: After this there are no more comments I swear.

comments.author: DBodesheim
comments.body:
Oh yes, I totally overlooked the _en-dash_ that appears! Thanks!

One final style question before I make the changes: should the $ sign be in front of the command to indicate that it should be executed in the command line? Because if it is kept in there, the $ sign stays copyable which is slightly annoying if one just quickly wants to copy the whole command. 
I saw that in the [documentation of the GUI](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/master/doc/ase/gui/basics.rst?ref_type=heads&plain=1) the $ is just kept there.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Maybe some sphinx-gallery tutorials already have shell commands done in a particular way?  Then we can do the same.

I notice that https://ase-lib.org/examples_generated/gettingstarted/00-n2cu.html#sphx-glr-examples-generated-gettingstarted-00-n2cu-py has an code block which is a shell command (`python N2Cu.py`) and it isn't possible to see from the formatting, only from the *content* and *context*, that it's something other than python.  That's a little bit unfortunate, I guess sphinx-gallery isn't really made to run other things than python snippets.

So some way of including the snippet that also has `$` [EDIT: or some other way of telling it apart from python] would be nice.  But please do what you think is best in the context.  We can make it consistent later if we find a better way.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Also this one has omitted the `$`: https://ase-lib.org/examples_generated/tutorials/acn.html#sphx-glr-examples-generated-tutorials-acn-py

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: I opened #1825 for things that we need to think about in a broader context, so meanwhile we just solve it any way that comes to mind.
